producer.name: performance_classification.py
limits: This record binds the PFP-0 classification and its declared identity; it executes nothing.
It does not establish that the cited campaign occurred as described; the campaign receipt is the record of that.
It does not turn a virtualised-court ratio into a frontier result, and it does not measure constant time.
A green validation is a statement about claim form, not about the truth of the measurement.

instrument.name: bench_api.c with alloc_probe.c and analyse_bench_api.py
measures: single-operation latency, median of five timed batch means per process
allocation entry points per operation through one LD_PRELOAD probe applied to both subjects
cross-library ECDSA correctness in both directions

samples.location: the campaign workspace raw/ directory (rep-*.out, run-order.tsv, identity checks); not committed
samples.obligation: The raw process outputs were retained in the campaign workspace, not committed to the repository; only the analysed result, receipt and cross-verification table are tracked.
samples.unit_of_replication: one process per subject per repetition
samples.statistic: median of paired per-repetition ratios candidate_us/authority_us

population.completeness_rule: A process is complete only when its RESULT and ALLOC lines match the exact frozen identifier set, once each; equal line counts are not a completeness test.

scope.security_profile: OpenSSL 3.6.4 production build as authority (linux-x86_64, assembly enabled, legacy provider enabled, no tests) against the candidate distribution-shaped libcrypto.so.3; default provider paths for the measured rows
exclusions: L1 and L2 arithmetic kernels are not measured separately
L4 protocol and L5 downstream workloads are not measured
throughput, tail latency, parallel scaling, peak RSS, energy, startup, cache and branch behaviour are not measured
constant-time behaviour is not measured; the threat model records an obligation, not a result
AWS-LC, BoringSSL, rustls and wolfSSL are not executed and give no comparison row

threat_model.statement: Private exponents, RSA private operands and ECDSA nonces and keys are SECRET_DATA; moduli and bases are public. The measured operations must not branch, address or exit early on secret values. This record binds the measurement; the timing obligations T23, T24 and T29 remain open.
threat_model.observation_model: wall-clock latency on a virtualised host; no PMU, no cache or branch counters, no frequency, turbo or SMT control

venue.description: virtualised court container on a 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900K, kernel 7.3.5-2-cachyos, pinned to one CPU; the PMU probe records cpu_event_source=absent

open.description: Secret ownership does not propagate through the arithmetic itself; the transfer window and 17 inversion intermediates at secret-dependent width remain open.
The constant-time inversion's scratch storage and the operands' normalised limb-count metadata remain the recorded residual.
The ECDSA per-signature allocation blow-up and the related fixed-width workspace residual remain open.
The venue exposes no PMU and has no frequency, turbo, SMT or isolation control; every row is SCOPED_OBSERVATION and no frontier claim is made.
The raw process outputs are not committed; the record binds the analysed result and receipt only.
AWS-LC, BoringSSL, rustls and wolfSSL were not executed; their rows are UNAVAILABLE or NOT_APPLICABLE, never losses.
Throughput, tail latency, parallel scaling, memory, energy, startup and L1/L2/L4/L5 behaviour are outside this record.
